query: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) is an unmodified α + β dual-phase alloy whose low hardness and poor friction and wear properties limit its use under extreme-service and high-contact-stress conditions. Formulate one hypothesis for an intervention that could improve its hardness and wear resistance without sacrificing its existing beneficial properties. State the intervention, proposed mechanism, predicted outcome relative to untreated TC4, applicable operating or test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) treated sequentially with a surface nanocrystallization process via severe plastic deformation (shot peening) followed by a low-temperature nitriding treatment will exhibit improved surface hardness and wear resistance relative to untreated TC4 while maintaining its bulk properties.
generation.material_initial_state: Unmodified TC4 (Ti6Al4V) dual-phase alloy with a coarse surface microstructure and limited hardness and wear resistance.
generation.intervention: Surface nanocrystallization through shot peening followed by low-temperature nitriding treatment.
generation.conditions: High-contact-stress and friction conditions, tested at room temperature and moderately elevated temperatures up to approximately 250°C.
generation.structural_mediator: A refined nanostructured surface layer accompanied by the formation of a superficial titanium nitride phase.
generation.mechanism: Shot peening refines the grain structure at the surface via the Hall-Petch effect, increasing hardness, while the low-temperature nitriding chemically converts the surface to a hard nitride layer, thereby enhancing wear resistance without affecting the alloy’s core properties.
generation.predicted_outcome: The treated TC4 is expected to show a significant increase in surface hardness and a reduced wear rate compared to untreated TC4 while preserving its bulk mechanical properties such as toughness and ductility.
generation.baseline: Performance metrics (e.g., surface hardness and wear rate) of untreated TC4 under the same testing conditions.
generation.boundary: The improvements are expected under conditions of high contact stress and friction at temperatures up to around 250°C. The behavior under significantly higher temperatures or cyclic fatigue conditions remains unverified.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of hardness improvement and wear resistance enhancement, along with long-term stability under repeated stress, remains uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare three sets of TC4 samples: (a) untreated control, (b) samples with only shot peening, and (c) samples with the combined shot peening and low-temperature nitriding treatment. Subject all samples to standardized hardness tests, wear tests (e.g., using a pin-on-disc setup), and microstructural analysis under high-contact-stress conditions at room temperature and up to 250°C.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the samples receiving the combined treatment do not exhibit at least approximately a 20% improvement in surface hardness and a corresponding reduction in wear rate compared to untreated TC4, or if there is a measurable detrimental change in bulk mechanical properties such as toughness, the hypothesis is considered falsified.

drafts.hypothesis: A dual intervention that first refines the surface microstructure through a severe plastic deformation treatment (e.g., shot peening) followed by a low-temperature nitriding process will enhance the hardness and wear resistance of TC4 (Ti6Al4V) without compromising its core beneficial properties.
drafts.material_initial_state: Unmodified TC4 (Ti6Al4V) α+β dual-phase alloy with coarse surface grains and limited wear properties.
drafts.intervention: Apply a surface nanocrystallization technique (severe plastic deformation via shot peening) to refine the grain structure, then perform a low-temperature nitriding treatment to form a thin, hard nitride layer on the surface.
drafts.conditions: Tests under high-contact-stress and friction conditions at ambient and moderately elevated temperatures (up to approximately 250°C) that are representative of extreme-service environments.
drafts.structural_mediator: A refined nanostructured surface coupled with the formation of a superficial titanium nitride (TiN) phase.
drafts.mechanism: Severe plastic deformation induces grain refinement at the surface, which increases hardness and strength by the Hall-Petch mechanism, while the nitriding process chemically converts the surface to a hard TiN layer. This combination is expected to improve wear resistance by providing a protective barrier without significantly affecting the alloy’s bulk properties.
drafts.predicted_outcome: The treated TC4 is expected to show a significantly increased surface hardness (tentatively in the range of 50–100% improvement) and improved wear resistance relative to untreated TC4, while retaining properties such as toughness and ductility in the underlying material.
drafts.baseline: Performance metrics (hardness, wear rates) of untreated TC4 under the same testing conditions.
drafts.boundary: The improvements are expected to hold under typical extreme-service conditions (high contact stresses, friction and wear tests) at temperatures up to around 250°C; effects at significantly higher temperatures or under cyclic fatigue load remain uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare three sets of TC4 samples: (a) untreated control, (b) samples with only shot peening (nanocrystallization), and (c) samples with the combined shot peening and low-temperature nitriding treatment. Subject all samples to standardized hardness tests (e.g., nanoindentation), wear tests (e.g., pin-on-disc), and microstructural analysis (via SEM/TEM and XRD) under high-contact-stress conditions at room temperature and at up to 250°C.
measurements: Wear rate measurements (mass loss or volume loss in pin-on-disc tests)
Phase identification and depth profiling with XRD
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the combined treatment samples do not exhibit at least approximately 20% improvement in both surface hardness and wear resistance compared to untreated TC4, or if the treatment detrimentally alters the alloy’s bulk mechanical properties (e.g., significant reduction in toughness), then the hypothesis is considered falsified.
